subject: Moderation impact on tool-calling — exception request & timeline
messages:
From: Sara Ortiz <sara.ortiz@finbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finbank.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0500
Subject: Moderation impact on tool-calling & structured output — exception request

Marcus —

Quick note from our security and platform teams: last Friday we had two production incidents where Redwood's content moderation layer rejected valid structured outputs from our policy-enforcement tool calls. The rejections triggered a fallback flow that returned generic "unable to complete" responses to end users for ~9 minutes and caused three downstream timeouts in our orchestration layer.

We need:
- A timeline for what happened (logs/trace) for 2026-11-13 02:00–04:00 UTC
- An explanation for why structured outputs were flagged (model / rule set / threshold)
- A request for a temporary SLA carve-out for tool-calling and structured output failures while we test the remediation you propose (we'd prefer explicit language covering fallback-induced client errors and an agreed notification cadence)

We're not asking for removal of moderation — just a contract amendment that accounts for tool-call fallbacks triggered by moderation during the pilot. Can you send the evidence and a proposed amendment text by end of week?

Thanks,
Sara Ortiz
Head of Platform Security
FinBank

--
FinBank internal reference: INC-2026-11-13-1087

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ortiz <sara.ortiz@finbank.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Moderation impact on tool-calling & structured output — exception request

Sara — thanks for the clear summary and the incident reference. I appreciate the urgency.

Quick notes / immediate actions:
- Attaching a sanitized extract of moderation hits and the request trace for 2026-11-13 02:00–04:00 UTC (filtered-logs-20261117.csv). We've redacted PII but preserved signal for rule IDs and confidence scores.
- Initial root cause (high level): an overlapping policy rule that treats certain JSON schema keys ("payment_reference") as sensitive heuristically. The rule triggered on a small subset of tool-call outputs that matched a heuristic pattern we use to catch unredacted payment tokens. The heuristics are rule-priority based and in this case outranked the structured-output exception because of a recent rule rollout on 11/12.
- Why fallback occurred: service-level policy routing bubbled the request to the moderation-fastpath which returns a 403 -> our tool-calling runtime then executes the configured fallback (we return a safe default string and mark the call as failed). That default response is surfaced to the app and caused the timeouts you saw.

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
1) Immediate: we can apply a scoped policy override for the FinBank tenant that widens the structured-output allowlist for the affected schema keys (overnight patch) — ETA 24 hours.
2) Near-term: we'll revert the rule priority change that caused the conflict and add a targeted unit test in our policy CI (3–5 days).
3) Contract: attach proposed wording for a temporary carve-out (see attached PDF) that covers tool-call failures driven by moderation rule conflicts during a 60-day remediation window. The carve-out also includes an obligation on our side to provide incident timelines within 48 hours and weekly status updates.

I am looping in Lauren (legal) and Soojin (runtime lead) to confirm the contractual language and the mitigation plan.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: filtered-logs-20261117.csv (CSV, redacted), proposed_sla_amendment_finbank_v1.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Moderation impact on tool-calling & structured output — exception request

Sara / Marcus —

I've reviewed Marcus's draft amendment. A few suggested edits from legal/procurement to keep in mind:
- Scope the carve-out to "moderation rule conflicts that result in deterministic runtime fallback responses for tool-calling and structured output formats"; avoid open-ended language about "any moderation event".
- Limit the carve-out duration to a negotiated remediation window (we proposed 60 days in the attached) with automatic re-evaluation at 30 days.
- Require Redwood to provide: incident timeline within 48 hours, sanitized logs (as provided), and a rollout plan for the fix.
- Exclude bad-faith bypass requests: if FinBank requests policy overrides that would disable required regulatory checks (e.g., SAR, sanctions), those are out of scope.

Operational note (Soojin) — can you confirm the ETA for the scoped policy override and the test coverage item? If we can commit to the 24h patch, this should materially reduce customer impact.

If Sara is comfortable, we can prepare a short DocuSign amendment for a 60-day carve-out with the clauses above and a pilot schedule.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
